4B.01.t: Volar Approach to the Distal Radius — FCR (Modified Henry)
4B.01.b:
### Step by step
[[FIG: Fig 4B.2 · 4B.01
- Position → supine, **forearm supinated** · Incision → 8 cm on the **radial border of FCR** (flexor carpi radialis)
  [[FIG: Fig 4B.3 · 4B.01
- Plane → distal Henry = **BR (brachioradialis; radial) / FCR (median)**; modified = **FCR sheath**, ulnar to the radial artery

1) Open the FCR sheath and floor → FCR retracted, **FPL** (flexor pollicis longus) swept ulnar
2) **L-shaped PQ** (pronator quadratus) cut: horizontal at the **watershed line**, vertical on the radial border
3) Styloid won't reduce → release **BR** from it
4) Plate **at or proximal** to the watershed line; joint screws checked on a lateral **tilted 20–25°**

- Danger → **radial artery** (radial side) → stay in the sheath · **palmar cutaneous branch** of median (ulnar) → don't stray ulnar to FCR
- Danger → **FPL** rubs on a plate past the watershed line · extensor tendons → dorsal screws **2 mm shorter** than measured

PITFALL — which way does FCR go?
- AO → FCR retracted **ulnarly** · Campbell's volar plate technique → **radially**
- Say → "either is fine; the **radial artery stays radial, the median nerve ulnar**"

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "volar approach to the distal radius"
- Supine, supinated → incision on the **radial border of FCR**
- FCR sheath → FPL swept ulnar → **L-shaped PQ** release
- Plate **proximal to the watershed line** → else FPL rupture
- At risk → radial artery (radial), palmar cutaneous branch (ulnar), FPL, extensors (long screws)
- Extend → proximally into Henry (BR/FCR plane)

### Step by step
[[FIG: Fig 4B.4 · 4B.02
- Position → supine, **forearm pronated** · Incision → 8 cm straight over Lister's tubercle
  [[FIG: Fig 4B.5 · 4B.02
- Plane → **none** → all muscles PIN (posterior interosseous nerve)-supplied → go between compartments

- Perilunate → dorsal first → SL (scapholunate) and LT (lunotriquetral) fixed; volar → add an **extended CTR** (carpal tunnel release)

4B.04.t: Volar Approach to the Wrist — Carpal Tunnel Release
4B.04.b:
### Step by step
[[FIG: Fig 4B.8 · 4B.04
- Incision → **mini-palm**, in line with the **radial border of the ring finger**, distal wrist crease → Kaplan's line · plane → none
  [[FIG: Fig 4B.9 · 4B.04

1) Palmar fascia → TCL (transverse carpal ligament)
2) Dissector between TCL and nerve → cut on the **ulnar side** of the nerve, a strip left on the hamate hook
3) Proximal end → distal antebrachial fascia **under vision**, never blind
4) Distal → stop at the **deep palmar fat** (= complete release)

- Danger → **motor branch** (radial side) → see it before cutting · **palmar cutaneous branch** (ulnar to FCR) → ring finger axis · **superficial palmar arch** (5–8 mm distal to the TCL edge) · ulnar nerve/artery → stay radial to the hook
- Rheumatoid synovectomy → FPL rupture over a **scaphoid spur** = Mannerfelt syndrome (Nagah p19)
- Failure → incomplete release, scar, neuroma, wrong diagnosis or level, double crush (Nagah p37)

PITFALL — where to cut the skin?
- Hoppenfeld → just ulnar and parallel to the thenar crease · Campbell → **ring finger axis**
- Say → "**in line with the radial border of the ring finger**, ulnar to the thenar crease"

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "carpal tunnel release — safe steps"
- Incision → ring finger axis, distal crease to Kaplan's line
- TCL cut on the **ulnar side** of the nerve → motor branch is radial
- Distal limit → palmar fat → superficial arch beyond
- Strip left on the hamate hook → flexors don't sublux ulnar
- Check the motor branch: extra-, sub- or transligamentous

4B.07.t: First Dorsal Compartment Release — de Quervain
4B.07.b:
### Step by step
[[FIG: Fig 4B.13 · 4B.07
- Incision → oblique along EPB preferred

1) Dermis only → blunt spread → protect **SRN** and LABC (lateral antebrachial cutaneous)
2) Open on the **dorsoulnar** side → keep a volar flap
3) Release **EPB first**, then APL (abductor pollicis longus) → find the **septum**
4) Pull test → thumb **extension + abduction** = complete

- No forceful wrist flexion for **2 weeks** → no tendon subluxation

EXAM PEARL — failed de Quervain release (Nagah p37; Campbell)
- Missed **EPB subcompartment** or aberrant tendon · **SRN** neuroma or adhesion
- Sheath opened volarly → **volar subluxation** of the tendons
- Wrong diagnosis → CMC (carpometacarpal) or STT (scaphotrapeziotrapezoid) arthritis, intersection syndrome

4B.10.t: Drainage of Pus in the Hand
4B.10.b:
### Principles
[[FIG: Fig 4B.21 · 4B.10
- Proximal block, **never local**; elevate, **no exsanguinating bandage**; see every bundle, leave wounds open

### Incisions — superficial infections
[[FIG: Fig 4B.22 · 4B.10
| Infection | Incision | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Paronychia** | Short cut at the nail-fold corner | Spare the nail bed |
| **Felon** | **Lateral**, dorsal to the DIP (distal interphalangeal) crease end → across the septa | Avoid ulnar thumb, radial index/middle (pinch) |
| **Web space** | Curved transverse **volar** ± dorsal | Never a longitudinal cut **through** the web |

PITFALL — felon and web space incisions
- Felon → Hopp: lateral · Campbell: **vertical midline** if it points volar
- Say → "drain where it points, **keep off the pinch surface**, never split the web"

### Tendon sheath, deep spaces & bursae
[[FIG: Fig 4B.23 · 4B.10
| Target | Incision | Key point |
|---|---|---|
| **Flexor sheath** | Proximal at the distal palmar crease + distal midlateral over P2 (middle phalanx) → catheter irrigation | Opens proximal to A1 and **distal to A4** |
| **Midpalmar** | Curved, just proximal to the distal palmar crease | Enter beside the **ring** flexor |
| **Thenar** | Just ulnar to the thenar crease or 1st web dorsal | **Motor branch** at the proximal end |
| **Radial bursa** | Lateral thumb P1 + wrist | Median nerve approached from the **radial** side |
| **Ulnar bursa** | Ulnar little finger P2 + hypothenar/wrist | Never cut blindly onto the probe |
| **Parona's space** | Volar forearm just above the crease | Drains a **horseshoe** abscess |

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "drainage of a flexor sheath infection"
- Kanavel signs → flexed, fusiform, tender along the sheath, pain on passive extension (→ 4A 4.12)
- Two incisions → **proximal** (A1 region, distal palmar crease) + **distal** midlateral at P2
- Catheter → through-and-through irrigation
- Keep **A2 and A4**; never a volar midline cut over the sheath
- Thumb or little finger → check the bursae and Parona's space

4B.14.b:
### Pins & wires — safe zones
[[FIG: Fig 4B.29 · 4B.14
- Distal third radius → **lateral / dorsoradial** half pins → radial artery in front, **SRN always near** · proximal third → none (PIN) · radius pins **between ECRL and ECRB** (extensor carpi radialis brevis)

MUST-KNOW — 60-second answer: "where do you put the distal radius ex-fix pins?"
- Radius → **8 cm above the wrist**, mini-open, **between ECRL and ECRB** (Campbell)
- SRN emerges between BR and ECRL → see it, protect it
- Metacarpal → **2nd MC base**, dorsoradial, 2 pins
- Never blind in the proximal third (PIN)
- Frame off at ≈6 weeks (Campbell)
- Pin <1/3 of bone width → 3 mm hand, 4 mm forearm; ≥2 per fragment (Clinical sheet)
